title: The first minute at work
hookLine: a breath before the first task: in Genesis, God breathes life into the man before the garden needs tending
tomorrow: why did Plato freeze with his hand raised in the air?

lines: A RED BADGE ON THE INBOX.
cards: The first thing touched at work is often not the work. It's the inbox: a red badge, a pile of overnight messages, and the day starts already behind. Genesis has a first workday too.

Before the man in the garden is given any job at all, the King James Version says: "And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul."

teach.b: Breath first. Only after that does the job arrive: the garden, "to dress it and to keep it."
In the order of the story, no one works before they breathe, and the breath is a gift before anything is asked. Jewish morning prayer keeps that order.

Among the Talmud's blessings for waking up is a thanks for the soul, the neshamah, the same word Genesis uses for the breath of life: my God, the soul you placed in me is pure; you breathed it into me.
The breath comes back each morning, and it's thanked as the day begins. Yesterday asked which parts of a rule travel to work: the ones that fit honest hours.
Here is the smallest piece that fits anywhere, at a desk, a till or a hospital station: before the first task, a breath. Not a long sit.
One breath, noticed, in the order Genesis gives it: breath, and then the work.

how: Jewish morning prayer includes the blessing Elohai neshamah, thanks for the soul breathed into a person, from the Talmud's blessings on waking (Berakhot 60b). On a personal rule, the first minute at work can be one noticed breath before the first task.

games.q: what does “the first minute at work” mean?
o: arriving early to get ahead of everyone else
reading every message before you start your work
one breath before the first task of the workday

games.q: the rule goes to work: tap the pairs.
p: each tradition keeps its own door
God breathed, then gave the garden

s: in Genesis, the man is given work before he is given breath
God breathes into his nostrils the breath of life first; the garden comes after.
a Jewish morning blessing thanks God for the soul breathed into you
from the Talmud's waking blessings: the soul you placed in me is pure.
breath first means a long meditation before you can start work
here it's one breath, noticed, before the first task.

games.q: a new teacher is about to open her classroom door on the first day, with a line of kids outside. what fits Genesis's order?
o: one breath before she opens the door, then the work.
open at once; every second of the job counts.
make them wait while she does a long meditation.
games.why: in Genesis the breath of life comes before the garden and its work. one breath, then the task.

practice: Put both feet on the floor and let your hands go still. Take one full breath, noticing it arrive, as if it were being handed to you. Then let your breathing carry on by itself for the rest of the sit, with no task waiting.

wordCard.voice: The first minute at work: one breath before the first task. In Genesis, the breath comes before the job.

orig.note: Hebrew, Genesis 2:7: the breath of life.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: breath first, and then the inbox. The work can wait one breath.
